The C++ program: n defaults to 7, overridable by argv[1] parsed with std::atoi. It samples 2*n points of a spiral
(t = i/(n*2), radius = t, angle = 4*M_PI*t, point = (radius*cos(angle), radius*sin(angle))), pushes that single ring
into a polygon, calls mapbox::earcut<uint32_t>(polygon), and prints each returned index followed by a single space
(std::cout << idx << " "), with NO trailing newline. The spiral self-intersects, so earcut's fallback passes
(filterPoints -> cureLocalIntersections -> splitEarcut) are heavily exercised, as is the z-order hashed path once the
total vertex count exceeds 80 (i.e. n > 40).

#!/bin/bash
# Predict glibc atoi() == (int)strtol(s,NULL,10) and the wrapped int loop bound n*2,
# purely in bash, so we can spot cases that would make the triangulator slow.
source /tmp/fuzz/corpus.sh

wrap32() { # $1 = 64-bit value -> signed 32-bit
  local v=$1
  v=$(( v & 0xFFFFFFFF ))
  if (( v >= 0x80000000 )); then v=$(( v - 0x100000000 )); fi
  echo "$v"
}

predict() {
  local s="$1"
  # skip isspace(): space \t \n \v \f \r
  s="${s#"${s%%[!$' \t\n\v\f\r']*}"}"
  local sign=1 digits=''
  case "$s" in
    -*) sign=-1; s="${s:1}" ;;
    +*) s="${s:1}" ;;
  esac
  # greedy leading digits
  digits="${s%%[!0-9]*}"
  [[ "$s" == *[!0-9]* ]] || digits="$s"
  if [[ -z "$digits" ]]; then echo 0; return; fi
  local stripped="${digits##+(0)}"
  shopt -s extglob; stripped="${digits##+(0)}"; shopt -u extglob
  [[ -z "$stripped" ]] && stripped=0
  local v
  if (( ${#stripped} > 19 )); then
    v=SAT
  elif (( ${#stripped} == 19 )); then
    if (( sign == 1 )); then
      [[ "$stripped" > "9223372036854775807" ]] && v=SAT
    else
      [[ "$stripped" > "9223372036854775808" ]] && v=SAT
    fi
  fi
  if [[ "$v" == SAT ]]; then
    # strtol saturates: LONG_MAX -> (int)-1 ; LONG_MIN -> (int)0
    if (( sign == 1 )); then echo -1; else echo 0; fi
    return
  fi
  if (( sign == -1 )) && [[ "$stripped" == "9223372036854775808" ]]; then
    echo 0; return   # LONG_MIN -> low 32 bits are 0
  fi
  local n64=$(( sign * 10#$stripped ))
  wrap32 "$n64"
}

printf '%-4s %-14s %-14s %s\n' IDX n loopbound arg_hex
slow=0
for i in "${!ARGS[@]}"; do
  a="${ARGS[$i]}"
  n=$(predict "$a")
  lb=$(wrap32 $(( n * 2 )) )
  flag=''
  if (( lb > 8000 )); then flag='  <== POTENTIALLY SLOW'; slow=$((slow+1)); fi
  if [[ -n "$flag" ]]; then
    printf '%-4s %-14s %-14s %s%s\n' "$((i+1))" "$n" "$lb" "$(printf '%s' "$a" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d '\n' | tr -s ' ')" "$flag"
  fi
done
echo "total cases: ${#ARGS[@]}; potentially slow: $slow"

pass=0; fail=0; n=0
